learningObjectives: Use the Tracer tool to identify and isolate errors in Pega application runtime events.
Configure Tracer settings, breakpoints, and use developer tools to debug Constellation UI applications.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Tracer — Overview and Reading Events

elements.text: Like a flight recorder, Tracer records the sequence surrounding a fault. The final failed event may be a symptom, so inspect earlier events rather than assuming the last event is always or rarely the cause.

elements.description: Troubleshooting tool that traces events that led to an error during application runtime. Access: App Studio → hover lower-right corner → Toggle runtime toolbar. OR Dev Studio → Developer toolbar.
Each event is logged as a separate row. Gray = Activity processing. Orange = Events from flow, Decision, or declarative Rules. Light blue = PegaRULES database and cache operations.
Good and Fail describe processing-step outcomes, not unit-test assertion statuses.
items: FAIL — error occurred; a failed step may be only the LAST in a chain — trace backwards to find the root cause

elements.caption: Event colors classify Activity, Flow/Decision/declarative and database/cache operations. A failed event may be a downstream symptom; inspect its preceding sequence.

elements.description: Constellation uses stateless DX API requests. The Tracer results organize events by request ID to distinguish simultaneously active requests.
Key Tracer constraints to know before use:
items: ⚠ CAUTION: Tracer is resource-intensive and DRAMATICALLY slows application performance
Only ONE Tracer per operator, per node is allowed
Pause logging until ready to trace the specific section
Toolbar (upper-right corner): Pause, Clear, Save buttons

elements.description: Filter options to narrow Tracer output:
items: Filter by: event, event type, Ruleset, break Conditions
Can exclude local variables or view only activities (not their steps)
Selection options: Events to Trace, Break Conditions, General Options, Event Types to Trace, Rulesets to Trace

elements.description: A Tracer settings option (NOT a toolbar button). Stops the Tracer automatically when the system generates an error. Different from Breakpoints — Break Conditions are passive error-triggered stops; Breakpoints are manually placed on specific activities.

In a supported tracing context, a breakpoint pauses tracing and its processing thread at the configured activity event. Resume with Play; the source also describes automatic resumption after an hour. Breakpoints and Watch are unsupported for Service Rules and Constellation applications.

Monitors specific property value(s) for changes. Useful for tracing calculation consistency and value-change patterns. Tracer highlights the property change in YELLOW and shows the Property Inspector. NOT supported for Service Rules and Constellation applications.

elements.caption: Scoped capture and pause behavior, without an invented absolute production ban or session-replacement guarantee.

elements.description: Browser extension; adds Components tab to console. Select any element to highlight screen. Run $r.props.getPConnect() to view component metadata. Used for Constellation application UI debugging.

Free browser plugin; adds Redux tab. Logs every action (type and payload). Visualizes state changes. Inspect state tree at any point. Client-side Data Pages are NOT in Redux — stored in the datastore.

elements.term: Client-side Data Pages — NOT in Redux
elements.description: Client-cached Data Pages reside in the application datastore, not Redux. PCore.getDataPageUtils() logs cached-page information. PCore/PConnect APIs are unavailable in the App Studio shell; launch the Portal from Dev Studio for these methods.

items: Xray overlays screen metadata, field metadata and state properties.
DebugPegaAPI is a dynamic system setting: verbose DX API inputs, actions, error fields/descriptions/codes and exception numbers in Pega logs.
UI Inspector exposes UI hierarchy, metadata, field properties and View properties.

examPitfalls.title: Tracer dramatically slows performance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Tracer has substantial capture overhead. The source calls for narrow capture and pausing when unused; do not use it as the performance-analysis tool.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Limit capture to relevant events, pause when unused and assess operational impact before tracing.

examPitfalls.title: One Tracer per operator, per node
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how many simultaneous Tracer sessions an operator can run on a single node. Candidates say 'unlimited' or 'two (primary + debug).' Exactly one Tracer session is allowed per operator per node.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The source states one Tracer per operator per node; it does not specify which session survives an attempt to open a second one.

examPitfalls.title: Failed step ≠ root cause — trace backwards
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario shows an error flagged on Step 7 of a Tracer trace. Candidates identify Step 7 as the root cause. The failed step is often a downstream symptom — trace backwards through earlier events to find the actual root cause.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A failed step may only indicate the LAST step in a sequence of events. Trace backwards through the log to find the actual root cause.

examPitfalls.title: Breakpoints stop THREAD processing, not just logging
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what happens to other processing when a Tracer breakpoint triggers. Candidates say 'only logging pauses.' A breakpoint stops the entire thread — all processing on that thread halts, not just Tracer output.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A supported breakpoint pauses the affected thread. Play resumes it; the source also describes resumption after one hour.

examPitfalls.title: Breakpoints and Watch not supported for Constellation or Service Rules
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which rule type can use Watch Functions. Candidates include Constellation UI or Service Rules. Breakpoints and Watch Functions are explicitly not supported for Service Rules and Constellation applications.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Breakpoints and Watch are NOT supported for tracing Service Rules and applications that use the Constellation design system. Use React DevTools, Redux DevTools, and PCore utilities instead.

examPitfalls.title: Client-side Data Pages are NOT in Redux
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where Pega stores client-side cached Data Pages in Constellation. Candidates say 'Redux store.' Client-side Data Pages are stored in the application cache — not in Redux — confirming a React DevTools misconception.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Data Pages cached on the client side are NOT stored in Redux — they are in the application's datastore. Use PCore.getDataPageUtils() in the browser console to list them.

examPitfalls.title: Break Conditions vs Breakpoints — different triggers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions present both Break Conditions and Breakpoints and ask which stops on a system-generated error. Candidates confuse them. Break Conditions is the settings option that triggers when the system generates an error; Breakpoints trigger at a specific step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Break Conditions are error-triggered settings; breakpoints target configured activity events. Respect context restrictions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is troubleshooting a runtime issue in a Constellation application and wants to open the Tracer tool to monitor rule execution without navigating away from App Studio. How is the Tracer accessed from within App Studio?

options.text: Hover over the lower-right corner, toggle the Runtime toolbar, then select Tracer
Navigate to Configure > Application > Quality > Tracer
Open the Developer toolbar and click the Tracer icon
Click Actions > Tracer on the Rule form toolbar

practiceQuiz.hint: It's accessed via a toolbar toggle in the lower-right corner.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Runtime toolbar is the documented App Studio entry point.

optionExplanations.A: The Runtime toolbar is the documented App Studio entry point.
optionExplanations.B: The topic does not give this Quality menu path for Tracer.
optionExplanations.C: Developer toolbar is the described Dev Studio entry point instead.
optionExplanations.D: This Rule-form command is not the App Studio entry point requested.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Tracer log, what color indicates events from flow, Decision, or declarative Rules?

options.text: Orange
Gray
Light blue
Yellow

practiceQuiz.hint: Gray = Activities; Light blue = Database; the third color is for Rules-based events.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Orange identifies these Flow, Decision and declarative events.

optionExplanations.A: Orange identifies these Flow, Decision and declarative events.
optionExplanations.C: Light blue identifies database and cache operations.
optionExplanations.D: Yellow is the Watch property-change highlight, not this event category.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Tracer shows a Fail status on a specific step. What is the correct approach to find the actual root cause?

options.text: Trace backwards through earlier events in the log
The failed step is always the root cause — fix it directly
Clear the Tracer and run again to confirm the error
Set a breakpoint on the failed step and rerun

practiceQuiz.hint: A Fail status may only indicate the last step in a sequence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Earlier events can reveal the cause behind the failed symptom.

optionExplanations.A: Earlier events can reveal the cause behind the failed symptom.
optionExplanations.B: The failed step is not guaranteed to be the root cause.
optionExplanations.C: Clearing first can discard the preceding diagnostic sequence.
optionExplanations.D: A breakpoint alone does not replace examining the earlier events.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A junior SA wants to leave the Tracer running in a shared testing environment to capture intermittent errors. What is the impact of running the Pega Tracer on application performance, and what is the recommended practice?

options.text: It significantly slows processing; capture only required events and pause when unused
It has minimal impact and can be left running in production
It only impacts performance when breakpoints are enabled
It temporarily pauses the application until tracing is complete

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish execution-event debugging from performance analysis.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capture overhead is significant; narrow events and pause when unused.

optionExplanations.A: Capture overhead is significant; narrow events and pause when unused.
optionExplanations.B: Minimal impact is not the source’s performance warning.
optionExplanations.C: Capture overhead exists without breakpoints too.
optionExplanations.D: Ordinary tracing does not inherently pause all application processing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How many Tracers can one operator run simultaneously on a single node?

options.text: One
Two — one for App Studio and one for Dev Studio
Unlimited
Three — one per thread

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a concurrent Tracer limit, not a stored-event-count limit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented limit is one per operator per node.

optionExplanations.A: The documented limit is one per operator per node.
optionExplanations.B: The two-studio distinction does not double the stated limit.
optionExplanations.C: Unlimited simultaneous Tracers contradict the stated limit.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not provide one Tracer per thread instead.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a non-Constellation, non-Service tracing context, a SendSimpleEmail activity breakpoint is reached. What happens to its processing thread?

options.text: The affected thread pauses; use Play to resume (the source also describes resumption after an hour)
Only logging pauses — the application continues processing
The Tracer clears all previous events and starts fresh
The system sends an error notification to the administrator

practiceQuiz.hint: Setting a Tracer breakpoint affects more than just logging — it pauses Case execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The affected thread pauses; Play resumes, with the source’s one-hour timeout.

optionExplanations.A: The affected thread pauses; Play resumes, with the source’s one-hour timeout.
optionExplanations.B: The breakpoint pauses thread execution as well as tracing.
optionExplanations.C: Clearing recorded events is not the stated breakpoint effect.
optionExplanations.D: An administrator notification is not the effect described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is configuring the Tracer to debug a Constellation UI application and asks a senior developer which Tracer features will not be available when working with Constellation. Which Tracer features are NOT supported when debugging Constellation applications?

options.text: Breakpoints and Watch Function
Pause and Clear buttons
Event type filtering
Ruleset-based filtering

practiceQuiz.hint: Two specific debugging features are restricted for Constellation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Breakpoints and Watch are the explicitly restricted features.

optionExplanations.A: Breakpoints and Watch are the explicitly restricted features.
optionExplanations.B: Pause and Clear are not the features excluded by this caution.
optionExplanations.C: Event filtering is not the excluded feature named here.
optionExplanations.D: Ruleset filtering is not the excluded feature named here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Watch Function is monitoring a property. In what color does the Tracer highlight a property value change?

options.text: Yellow
Orange
Green
Red

practiceQuiz.hint: A distinct highlight color is used to flag changes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Yellow is the stated property-change highlight.

optionExplanations.A: Yellow is the stated property-change highlight.
optionExplanations.B: Orange classifies a different event category.
optionExplanations.C: Green is not the Watch highlight specified by the source.
optionExplanations.D: Red is not the Watch highlight specified by the source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Constellation Portal launched from Dev Studio, which tool and command inspect a selected React component’s metadata?

options.text: React DevTools — select the element then run $r.props.getPConnect()
Redux DevTools — inspect the state tree
Xray tool — debug page instructions
Tracer Watch Function — monitor the component property

practiceQuiz.hint: React DevTools has a specific command for component metadata.
practiceQuiz.rationale: React DevTools and this component command expose the metadata.

optionExplanations.A: React DevTools and this component command expose the metadata.
optionExplanations.B: Redux inspects actions and state rather than this component command.
optionExplanations.C: Xray overlays metadata but is not the requested React command.
optionExplanations.D: Watch is restricted in Constellation and is not component inspection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Constellation Portal launched from Dev Studio, where are client-cached Data Pages stored, and how can you log them?

options.text: In the application's datastore — run PCore.getDataPageUtils() in the browser console
In Redux — inspect the Redux DevTools state tree
In the Pega Clipboard — use the Clipboard tool in Dev Studio
In the Tracer log — search for Data Page events

practiceQuiz.hint: Client-side Data Pages are managed in the browser directly, not stored in Redux state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The application datastore and PCore utility are the source’s answer.

optionExplanations.A: The application datastore and PCore utility are the source’s answer.
optionExplanations.B: These cached Data Pages are explicitly not stored in Redux.
optionExplanations.C: Server Clipboard is not this client-side datastore.
optionExplanations.D: Tracer events do not list the browser’s cached-page datastore.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When the DebugPegaAPI dynamic system setting is active, what information is saved to the Pega log files?

options.text: Input values, actions performed, error fields, error descriptions, error codes and exception numbers
React component hierarchy and Redux state changes
Tracer event logs including breakpoint hits
Unit test case results and assertion failures

practiceQuiz.hint: DebugPegaAPI dynamic system setting logs DX API call details to the Pega log files.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These inputs, actions and error details are logged by the dynamic setting.

optionExplanations.A: These inputs, actions and error details are logged by the dynamic setting.
optionExplanations.B: React and Redux inspection is a separate browser concern.
optionExplanations.C: This setting does not represent Tracer breakpoint-event logging.
optionExplanations.D: Unit assertion results are not the API debug fields described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Tracer filter option stops the Tracer automatically when the system generates an error?

options.text: Break Conditions
Breakpoints
Rulesets to Trace
Event Types to Trace

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a settings option, not a toolbar feature.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Break Conditions stop tracing on the selected system errors.

optionExplanations.A: Break Conditions stop tracing on the selected system errors.
optionExplanations.B: Breakpoints stop at configured activity events instead.
optionExplanations.C: Ruleset selection narrows capture, not this error trigger.
optionExplanations.D: Event-type selection narrows capture, not this error trigger.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is using the Tracer tool to investigate a runtime issue. Which TWO types of events can the Tracer monitor during Case processing?

options.text: Rule executions such as Data Transforms, Decision Tables, and Activities
Database queries generated during Case processing
User mouse-click events in the Constellation UI
Browser paint and layout timing from the browser Performance panel

practiceQuiz.hint: Tracer captures server-side rule execution and database activity — not front-end UI interactions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Server Rule executions are captured as processing events. Database processing is one of the captured event categories.

optionExplanations.A: Server Rule executions are captured as processing events.
optionExplanations.B: Database processing is one of the captured event categories.
optionExplanations.C: Browser mouse-click logs are not these server processing events.
optionExplanations.D: Browser paint/layout timing belongs to browser performance inspection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For a non-Constellation, non-Service tracing context, which TWO statements match the documented Tracer capabilities?

options.text: You can set breakpoints to pause Rule execution at a specific step for inspection
Tracer settings allow filtering by event type to reduce noise and focus on relevant rules
One operator can run unlimited concurrent Tracers on one node
The Tracer automatically identifies and applies fixes to any Rule errors it encounters

practiceQuiz.hint: Tracer offers breakpoints and event filtering — recall the operator-per-session restriction.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Supported breakpoints pause the affected execution thread. Event filtering reduces capture to relevant events.

optionExplanations.A: Supported breakpoints pause the affected execution thread.
optionExplanations.B: Event filtering reduces capture to relevant events.
optionExplanations.C: Unlimited concurrent Tracers violate the operator/node limit.
optionExplanations.D: Tracer helps diagnose events; it does not automatically repair Rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is debugging a Constellation UI application where a Data Transform is producing incorrect property values. Which TWO Pega tools are most appropriate for diagnosing this issue?

options.text: Tracer — to trace the Data Transform execution and inspect property values at each step
UI Inspector — to inspect UI hierarchy, component metadata, field properties and View properties
Pulse — to send a debugging message to the Case team about the issue
Report Builder — to create a report that shows all changed field values in the Case

practiceQuiz.hint: Pair server-side event tracing with documented UI metadata inspection; Watch/breakpoints are restricted in Constellation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Trace server execution events and inspect their property snapshots. UI Inspector supplies the stated UI metadata and property context.

optionExplanations.A: Trace server execution events and inspect their property snapshots.
optionExplanations.B: UI Inspector supplies the stated UI metadata and property context.
optionExplanations.C: Pulse collaboration does not inspect these execution or metadata details.
optionExplanations.D: Report Builder is not the tool for this live execution/metadata diagnosis.

Resource-intensive; DRAMATICALLY slows app. One per operator per node. Pause until needed.
